quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When your motorcycle is in another vehicle's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Stay where you are so you don't surprise the driver.
Wave at the other driver to get their attention.
Slow down and move out of the blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and move out of the blind spot.
questions.explanation: If you are in a vehicle's blind spot, either speed up quickly or slow down to leave the spot.

questions.question: How should a group of riders pass another vehicle on a two-lane highway?
questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time.
questions.explanation: Riders should pass one at a time. The next rider should wait until the first rider has safely returned to the original lane before starting to pass. Continue this pattern until all riders have passed.

questions.question: When carrying a heavy load, what should you adjust?
questions.correctAnswerText: The suspension.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a heavy load, set your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to the weight settings recommended by your motorcycle manufacturer.

questions.question: Which type of sign is usually rectangular?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black text or symbols. You must follow all rules on these signs.

questions.question: Why is riding directly alongside another vehicle dangerous?

options.text: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
It is safer than riding behind the vehicle.
It is safe because it limits your escape routes.
You should only do this during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle puts you in its blind spot. The driver may not see you and could change lanes without warning. This position also blocks your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Where should a load be placed on a motorcycle?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them in saddlebags. Placing loads high on the frame or sissy bar raises the center of gravity and affects balance. Distribute weight equally on both sides.

questions.question: Why should a load be placed low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
You may not see over a high load.
Other drivers cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Placing a load too high raises your motorcycle's center of gravity and makes it harder to balance.

questions.question: Which of these will NOT help you avoid accidents?

options.text: Spotting hazards and deciding which to handle first.
Keeping space between you and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding without a headlight.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, stay alert and ready to react. Spot hazards and decide how to handle them. Always use your headlight to be more visible, and maintain space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Move to the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden movements, stay away from the road edge, and ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handle grips.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold both handle grips firmly, ease off the throttle, and keep a straight course. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake of the tire that is still good. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what is the best way to stay close together while keeping a safe distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps the group close while giving each rider safe space. Use a single-file line when riding on curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side with another rider.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the rear of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them and help if needed.

questions.question: What color vest or jacket helps you be seen best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to be seen better. Bright red, orange, yellow, or green work best. Dark colors are harder to see.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors, what should you focus on?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and the lane next to you. You may see a bit of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and to the side is most important.

questions.question: What happens when your rear tire skids?

options.text: You lose the ability to change direction.
It is only a problem if the front tire also skids.

questions.correctAnswerText: You lose the ability to change direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a serious crash. When you use too much rear brake, the wheel locks and you cannot change direction. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: What can happen if you shift to a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: Your motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may lurch and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may lurch and a warning light will go on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear while going too fast, your motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid. This causes you to lose control. Always slow down before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: What should you do if you must ride over an obstacle?

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Stay on your seat and remove your feet from the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down and hit it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep your motorcycle straight. Just before hitting it, ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: What is true about approved helmets?

options.text: They can limit how far you can see.
They let you see as far to the sides as you need.
You do not have to wear one if it limits your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: They let you see as far to the sides as you need.
questions.explanation: Some people worry that helmets limit vision, but this is not true. Approved helmets let you see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.

questions.question: A person drinks seven drinks in three hours. The body removes about one drink per hour. How many drinks are likely in their system three hours after their last drink?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: To estimate drinks remaining, subtract the hours since the last drink from the total drinks consumed. In this case: 7 drinks consumed minus 6 hours (3 hours drinking plus 3 hours after) equals about 4 drinks remaining.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding alongside another rider?

options.text: It lets you use more of the road.
It makes it easier to talk to them.
It makes it easier for other vehicles to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: It limits your escape routes.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another motorcycle because it limits both riders' escape routes if a hazard appears.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's total braking power comes from the front brake?
questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When stopping, what should you do?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only one brake, either front or rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time.

questions.question: Which material offers the best protection for motorcyclists?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather provides the best protection for motorcyclists. Always wear clothing that covers your legs and arms completely when riding.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
Apply both brakes hard while still leaning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
questions.explanation: First straighten your motorcycle and square the handlebars, then stop. If you cannot straighten the motorcycle, apply the brakes smoothly and gradually. Reduce your lean angle and increase brake pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting to first gear, you may need to:

options.text: Slow down with your brakes before downshifting safely.
Flash your brakes so drivers behind know you are downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down with your brakes before downshifting safely.
questions.explanation: Before shifting to a lower gear, slow down enough to shift safely. Downshifting too fast can cause the motorcycle to jerk and the rear wheel to skid. Use the brakes to reach a safe speed before downshifting.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Guarantees the other driver will yield to you.
Does not mean the driver will yield to you.
Means the driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean the driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact means another driver will yield the right-of-way to you.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this will make the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle to slow down. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Avoid braking, as it may worsen the wobble.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Try to squeeze into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger's weight affects your motorcycle's handling. Your motorcycle will accelerate slower, turn slower, and need more distance to stop. Ride more slowly, slow down sooner, keep a larger space cushion, and wait for bigger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: Which formation is best for keeping a group of riders close together?
questions.correctAnswerText: Staggered
questions.explanation: A staggered formation helps a group stay close while letting each rider maintain safe spacing. Use a single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while riding, what happens?

options.text: The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering will feel heavy.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire causes heavy steering. If your steering feels heavy, exit the road immediately and check your tires.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless it is raining.
Should always be avoided because other parts of the lane do not have it.
Improves traction for most motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil drips from cars collect in a strip down the center of a lane. When the road is dry, this area gives enough traction for motorcyclists to ride safely. The strip is usually only about two feet wide, so you can often ride to one side of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the opposite direction of where you want to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
questions.explanation: If you need to swerve to avoid something, press the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then the right to straighten. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: When another vehicle is following you too closely, you should:

options.text: Let the other driver pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the other driver pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If you can do it safely, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up can make things more dangerous by encouraging them to tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the alcohol was consumed
How often a person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often a person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect blood alcohol content: how much alcohol was consumed, how fast it was consumed, and body weight. Gender, physical condition, and food intake may also have some effect.

questions.question: During a pre-ride inspection, you should check everything except the:
questions.correctAnswerText: Reflectors.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your motorcycle carefully. Inspect the tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch and throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle:

options.text: You may drive faster than the speed limit until the pass is done.
You may ignore "No passing zone" signs if you started the pass in a legal zone.
You may pass on the shoulder.
You must complete the pass within the speed limit and in a legal passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must complete the pass within the speed limit and in a legal passing zone.
questions.explanation: You must finish a pass within the posted speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: When riding in a group, motorcyclists should:

options.text: Cut their normal space cushions in half.
Keep adequate space cushions around each rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep adequate space cushions around each rider.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close but keep enough space around each rider to stop safely if needed.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo:

options.text: It takes less time to speed up but more time to stop.
It takes more time to speed up and stop.
It takes more time to speed up but less time to stop.
It takes less time to speed up and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes more time to speed up and stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo makes your motorcycle slower to speed up and stop compared to riding alone.

questions.question: For normal braking, you should:

options.text: Switch between front and rear brakes to make them last longer.
Always use both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use both the front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When entering a highway or curve, a group of motorcyclists should:

options.text: Ride along the far right of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride single-file.
questions.explanation: While a staggered formation is usually best, switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side of the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Do not ride in the center of the lane when it is wet. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is often the best choice.

questions.question: What is true about a windshield?

options.text: It can replace a face shield.
It does not fully protect your eyes from the wind.
It is required on all motorcycles.
You should use it only on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not fully protect your eyes from the wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from the wind.

questions.question: When weight moves to the front of your bike while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Gradually increase pressure on the front brake.
Do not worry. The weight transfer will not affect your motorcycle.
Try to lock the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gradually increase pressure on the front brake.
questions.explanation: As your bike slows down, weight moves forward to the front tire. Gradually increase front brake pressure as this happens.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab at the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam on the front brake and grab at the rear brake.
Press down on the front brake and jam on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the front brake lever and press down on the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes together when slowing or stopping.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: After at least an hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts riding.

questions.question: When should you use the front brake?

options.text: Any time you are slowing or stopping
Only when slowing or stopping on slippery roads
Only when slowing or stopping in an emergency
Only when slowing or stopping in traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you are slowing or stopping
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When making a turn, what happens to traction?

options.text: There is less traction available for stopping.
There is more traction available for stopping.
Stopping is the same as on a straightaway.
You should never try to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is less traction available for stopping.
questions.explanation: When a motorcycle is leaning to turn, some traction is used for turning. This leaves less traction available for braking.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use quick pressure on the front brake to prevent locking the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the front brake lever slowly to avoid locking the front wheel and use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: What will help you ride safely on slippery surfaces?
questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed and use both brakes. Avoid sudden movements and the center of the lane. Follow tire tracks left by cars. Watch for hazards like oil spots and loose gravel.
